data.narrative:
Project Omega, a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Stafford Sheehan, has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector comp universe of 11 total peers—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private—including established players like Helion, Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, X-Energy, and Valar Atomics.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables; the nuclear energy sector yields only one same-stage peer and one adjacent-stage peer, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold needed for reliable median pricing. A stage-progression approach is therefore the primary method: applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next stage against the $12M raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $30M. This multiplier reflects typical progression mechanics for early-stage frontier-tech companies advancing from seed funding.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered on $30M. The median estimate carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method; the nuclear energy sector's nascent state and heterogeneity among peers (ranging from modular reactor designs to fuel technology) limit direct comparability. Further validation would benefit from closer inspection of revenue traction, capital intensity, and timeline-to-commercial deployment across the peer set. The wide range also reflects seed-stage inherent variance and the absence of sufficient transactional data within Project Omega's immediate peer band.
